visible_observation: The composition is currently split into two distinct, disconnected zones: a heavy typographic block anchored in the top-left and a sparse, geometric illustration floating in the center-right. The text and the visual elements (the glowing nodes and jellyfish) occupy separate planes without overlapping or interacting, creating a 'list' layout rather than a unified scene. The bottom text anchors are also widely separated, failing to create a cohesive base.
critique: The layout lacks spatial integration. The title 'BELOW THE LAST LIGHT' acts as a static label rather than an environmental element. Because the text and the illustration do not overlap or share a visual field, the poster reads as a text box next to a picture box, rather than a single atmospheric composition. The visual path is disjointed, jumping from the heavy text to the faint graphics without a connecting rhythm.
revision: Shift the typographic block to the right side of the canvas to balance the visual weight of the jellyfish on the left. Apply a 'multiply' blend mode or a dark gradient mask to the text so it fades into the background darkness, allowing the bioluminescent nodes to visually pass *behind* or *through* the letters. This will integrate the text into the deep-sea environment rather than having it sit on top of it.
protected_strength: The atmospheric lighting and the subtle, glowing cyan color palette effectively evoke the deep-sea environment and must be preserved.
